name: Latent-State Recruitment and Two Clocks of Adaptation
hypothesis: Heritable variants of a physically conserving ecology may recruit latent dynamical switching/relaxation capabilities already accessible to the substrate, giving rise to useful within-lifetime response spectra and changing their selection across generations, without an installed intelligence reward or memory API.
novelty_claim: New falsifiable cross-timescale comparison and operational tests, NOT claim of a newly demonstrated organism or newly invented general mathematical principle.

independent_observables.question: Which biophysical/program interaction states are possible in the ancestral substrate without model alteration?
independent_observables.null: developer secretly adds new reaction/opcode during test

independent_observables.question: Does an inherited change make an otherwise inaccessible latent behavior reachable?
independent_observables.null: passive environmental difference or preprogrammed switch

independent_observables.question: At fixed lineage genotype/current inputs, does temporal history change response reliably?
independent_observables.null: population sorting, instrument artifact, regression to mean

independent_observables.question: Does organism-mediated action alter a distribution of physical response times?
independent_observables.null: fixed fractional kernel/integral controller hardwired by evaluator

independent_observables.question: Does the inherited state interface improve held-out material viability after paying full switching cost?
independent_observables.null: novelty score, training target, time-correlated treatment label

independent_observables.question: Do daughters/granddaughters autonomously reproduce a functional collective state without external automatic group copying?
independent_observables.null: externally copied full agents or shuffled cohabitation

future_only_comparators: substrate chemistry with heritable access changes
unseen shift to different environment frequency
reject_conditions: positive effect explained fully by fixed feedback at same cost
no independent within-life history effect after genotype control
only 2009/2015 reused evolution dataset counted as multiple independent origins
model ribosomal subpopulation claimed experimentally proven without perturbation
relative metabolic current-growth benefit vanishes after accounting next-transition lag
new daughter phenotype supplied by engine copy instead of internal reproduction
behavior misleadingly interpreted as subjective consciousness
